output.problem: The bill states that the existing assistance law for private education (RA No. 6728 as amended by RA No. 8545) has become outdated and insufficient for current challenges. It cites a sharp fall in private school enrollment during the pandemic and the movement of teachers and students to public schools, which strains both sectors. It seeks to strengthen private basic education in its complementary role with public schools, with priority to the underprivileged.
output.problem_quote: the educational landscape has significantly evolved, rendering some of its provisions outdated and insufficient to address current challenges.

rows.differences: SB No. 1073 sets up the in-service training fund as a separate section with a stated purpose, a per capita ceiling tied to the public basic education fund, and DepEd approval of training programs; the bill lists the fund without purpose, ceiling or approval mechanism.
rows.why: The comparator's per capita ceiling and DepEd approval give the fund a defined limit and quality control, which the bill's open listing lacks; the revision is to keep it within Section 7 so the scholarship and institutional development items remain.
rows.tradeoffs: A ceiling makes the fund predictable but may limit training where private school teacher needs exceed public school levels.
rows.gap: The per capita level of in-service training funds for public basic education is not in the material and must be checked.

rows.target_quote: Provided, That the amount shall not be less than the amount currently provided by the DepEd
rows.differences: The related bills given carry the same voucher design, including the coverage of kindergarten to secondary, the minimum amount and the sixty-day payment period, so no real alternative is offered.
rows.why: No related measure offers a different design, and the minimum amount and payment period protect participating schools and students.
rows.tradeoffs: A floor on the voucher amount protects beneficiaries but removes flexibility to adjust amounts to available funds.
rows.gap: The current voucher amounts and the number of kindergarten and elementary students that would be newly covered are not in the material.

rows.target_quote: the government shall provide the teachers with salary subsidy, to be determined by the DepEd
rows.differences: No related measure in the material offers a different design for the salary subsidy fund.
rows.why: The fund responds directly to the teacher movement to public schools cited in the explanatory note, and no alternative design is given.
rows.tradeoffs: Leaving the subsidy amount to the DepEd gives flexibility but makes the recurring cost harder to estimate.
rows.gap: The subsidy amount, eligible teacher count and relation to any existing salary subsidy under RA No. 8545 cannot be established from the material.

rows.target_quote: to serve as the focal office for the administration, supervision, and regulation of all matters relating to private basic education institutions, including government assistance and subsidies.
rows.differences: All related bills given create the same bureau with the same powers and functions, so none offers a different composition, rank or attachment.
rows.why: A single focal office for private basic education matches the bill's purpose, and the material does not identify an existing office already performing these functions.
rows.tradeoffs: A dedicated bureau gives focus and accountability but adds a new organizational unit and staffing within the DepEd.
rows.gap: Whether existing DepEd offices already administer private education assistance and regulation, and the fit with RA No. 12231, must be checked.

rows.target_quote: The GASS shall serve as the permanent secretariat for the implementation of the GAS programs under this Act.
rows.differences: No related measure in the material offers a different council composition or administrative arrangement.
rows.why: Splitting policy guidance (council) from day-to-day administration (a service under the bureau) is a workable design and no alternative is given.
rows.tradeoffs: An inter-agency council adds oversight but meets only as needed, which may slow decisions on voucher amounts.

memo_part.heading: On the In-Service Training Fund
paragraphs: 4.1 Section 7 (Other Forms of Assistance) of the bill provides for an in-service training fund for teachers in participating private basic education schools, together with graduate scholarships and a program of institutional development assistance. It may be noted that the provision does not state the purpose of the fund, any limit on its amount, or the mechanism for approving the training programs it would finance.

4.2 In this regard, may we recommend that the provision be revised to specify the purpose of the fund and to provide that the amount available to private basic education shall not exceed that available to public basic education on a per capita basis, with training programs subject to DepEd approval, similar to Section 9 of SB No. 1073. This would align the assistance with the support given to public school teachers and provide a basis for programming the fund. We defer to the DepEd on the appropriate per capita reference.

self_critique.objection: Private school teachers are leaving for the public sector, so tying their training fund to the public per capita level may cap support exactly where the explanatory note says the need is greatest.
self_critique.condition: The ceiling holds only if the per capita reference covers the private teachers actually participating; the DepEd may need room to adjust it.

self_critique.objection: Section 15 (Transitory Provision) makes kindergarten and elementary implementation subject to available funds, which sits uneasily with the fixed floor and sixty-day payment in Section 8 and argues for a more flexible design.
self_critique.condition: Retention holds if Section 8 is read together with Section 15 so that the expanded coverage is phased in subject to available funds.

self_critique.objection: Because the amount is left entirely to the DepEd, the fund could become a large open-ended recurring commitment, and a stated basis would better support planning.

The bureau's assistance functions in Section 11(d) and the GASS in Section 12 both administer the same programs, and the material signals possible overlap with existing DepEd offices, which could justify removal.
self_critique.condition: Retention holds only if a review confirms no existing DepEd office already performs these functions.

self_critique.objection: The council in Section 12 sets higher voucher amounts under Section 4 while Section 8 leaves amounts to the DepEd, so the arrangement may create unclear lines of authority.

theory_of_change.problem: Private basic education is losing students and teachers, straining congested public schools.
theory_of_change.mechanism: Vouchers, teacher salary subsidies and training funds administered by a new DepEd bureau.
theory_of_change.outcome: Stronger private schools absorb learners from congested public schools and keep their teachers.
theory_of_change.weakest_assumption: That sufficient funds will be appropriated for expanded coverage and the minimum voucher floor.
